Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to up to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speaker's card available at the entry of the meeting room. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of items shown on the agenda.
THIS AGENDA HAS BEEN AMENDED TO INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING NOTICE: This meeting is being held pursuant to Executive Order N-25-20 issued by California Governor Gavin Newsom on March 12, 2020 to further the State's efforts to control the spread of COVID-19 Coronavirus. Any and all council members may attend and participate by teleconference/virtual meeting. Members of the public may also attend by teleconference in order to observe and provide public comment during the meeting. The meeting will not be livestreamed. If you wish to participate . . .

Public comments submitted electronically via email will be provided to the legislative body, but will not be read aloud at the meeting.
If you would like to address the City Council during the meeting, please email CityCouncilMeeting@pvestates.org with (1) your name, (2) the agenda item on which you'd like to speak, and (3) the phone number and/or Zoom name from which you will be calling in to the meeting. This will replace the in-person speaker cards.

  City Manager's Report

  Acting City Manager Rukavina reported, providing an update to the County's restrictions and
  re-opening guidelines.

  a.  State of the Police Department - Oral Report

  Interim Police Chief Dreiling reported on the progress of the Police Ad-hoc committee.

 MAYOR & CITY COUNCILMEMBERS' REPORTS

 Councilmernber Kao reported on looking into Emergency Preparedness training for elected officials,
 the Heroes Act, and the Clean Power Alliance as a future agenda item, and the Notice of Vacancies.

 Councilmernber Davidson acknowledged Memorial Day, Thanked John Harbison, requested to
 discuss term limits for City Council, and requested the City look into retaining a grant writer.

 Mayor Pro Tern Kemps requested the City research and issue a Request for Proposal for a grant writer,
 noted progress of the Pension Ad-hoc committee, expressed concerns regarding the Budget and
 expressed appreciation for lngo Hentschel at Cox Communications. He also requested review and
 discussion of the Council Meeting technology and recording procedures.

 CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
 May 26 , 2020
 Councilmember Lozzi expressed concern regarding the budget and reported that she was elected
Chair of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Transit Authority with Mayor Pro Tern Kemps as vice-chair. She
also reported on the progress of the Investment Poli cy Advisory Committee and requested a future
agenda item for George Allan field.

Mayor McGowan reported on the focus to re-open local businesses safely, and requested Acting City
Manager Rukavina's assistance with a letter of support for the recycled water project.

There being no further business to come before the Council, it was moved by Mayor Pro Tern Kemps
and seconded by Councilmember Kao to adjourn the meeting. The meeting was adjourned at 9:51
p.m. to the next regular meeting on June 9, 2020 at 6:30 p.m.
